title: "{stringr} rejects the empty pattern that grepl() accepts"
ref: STR-05
categories: [Strings]
impact: incoherent
extrait: 'grepl("", c("apple", "pear"))'
reponse: 'TRUE TRUE'
attendu: "the same result with `str_detect()`"
versions: "Since {stringr} 1.5.0; before that, `str_subset(x, \"\")` returned everything"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2023)"
---

::: {.piege packages="stringr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(stringr))

fruits <- c("apple", "pear")
pattern <- ""
grepl(pattern, x = fruits)
str_detect(fruits, pattern = pattern)
str_subset(fruits, pattern = pattern)
str_split(fruits, pattern = pattern)
```
:::

## Why

The empty pattern matches everywhere. Base R draws the logical conclusion: `grepl("", x)` is `TRUE` for every string. {stringr} did the same up to version 1.4. Since 1.5.0, `str_detect()`, `str_subset()`, `str_starts()` and `str_ends()` stop with an error, on the grounds that an empty pattern is almost always a bug.

The pitfall appears when the pattern comes from a variable, for example a search field left blank: a filter that used to keep everything starts failing after an upgrade. And not every function follows the rule: `str_split()` still accepts the empty pattern and splits into characters.

## The remedy

Handle the empty pattern explicitly, according to what it should mean.

::: {.piege packages="stringr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(stringr))

keep_matching <- function(x, pattern) {
  if (pattern == "") {
    return(x)
  }
  str_subset(x, pattern = pattern)
}
keep_matching(fruits, pattern = "")
keep_matching(fruits, pattern = "pp")
```
:::
